objective: Make verified Quest v2 objective progress, completion, and canonical reward commit atomically through one idempotent controller action, eliminating completed-without-reward partial state while preserving all existing actions, provenance, and player-state authority without changing the production database schema.

roles_before.artifact: All System writes pass through PostgreSQL system_apply_action or the behaviorally matched ephemeral store.
quest.complete appends a completion after required Quest v2 objectives are already complete.
progression.award is a separate verified write linked to a completion and checked against system-quest-reward:v1.
Each existing action has one Idempotency-Key and request-hash conflict boundary.
system_events is append-only and Neon remains the sole mutable owner of derived RPG state.
Existing quest.progress, quest.complete and progression.award actions remain available for compatibility and diagnostics.
A code deployment cannot itself create progress, completion, reward, profile, or other player events.
The production schema currently ends at migration 007; the authorized hourly maintenance loop does not permit autonomous production schema mutation.
Previous completion and award behavior remains recoverable from Git/deployment rollback.

role_dispositions.destination: Additive quest.resolve orchestration wraps the existing system_apply_action child actions in one PostgreSQL transaction; no new SQL function or migration is introduced.
The canonical quest.completed child event and all existing Quest v2 objective/terminal validation remain unchanged.
The canonical progression.awarded child event, verified-evidence requirement, one-award constraint and calibration trigger remain unchanged.

quest.resolve uses one root Idempotency-Key and full root request hash, derives stable collision-resistant child keys, and replays the committed child set on exact retry while changed root reuse conflicts before mutation.
Only ordinary validated quest.progressed, quest.completed and progression.awarded child events are appended; no update/delete or second state owner is introduced.
All existing action types and response behavior remain supported; quest.resolve is additive.
Deployment changes code only. No player event is created until a later explicitly authorized quest.resolve call.
No migration 008, table, trigger, index or function is added; production verification can remain read-only.
The base code remains in Git history and callers may continue using the previous separate actions after rollback.

capability_probes.assertion: quest.progress, quest.complete and progression.award retain their existing validation and response behavior.
An invalid or unverifiable resolution leaves no new progress, completion or reward event.
A scored resolution cannot award from merely reported objective progress; every required objective must be complete with verified latest progress.
Profile calibration, shop, deadline expiry, push delivery, Russian PWA session and legacy LifeUp regressions still pass.
The exact base SHA retains the previous separate completion/award flow and all existing production data remains compatible.

tests.expected: Verified quest.resolve appends final progress, completion and exact reward; exact retry replays; changed-key reuse conflicts; invalid resolution leaves no partial events.
Existing PostgreSQL action gate is composed inside one transaction; canonical reward is derived from the scored quest and exact retry does not duplicate events.
